parsed.attack: The embed channel and the audience are anticorrelated: gurdwaras, temples and community classes are run by and for the generation that already speaks the language, while the stated user is the twenty-something who has drifted away from exactly those institutions - that drift is the premise of the product, so the channel selects against the buyer. The one thing worth sharing, a named grandmother's recorded voice, is also the one asset useless to anybody else and slightly shameful to surface, since the confession embedded in it is 'I cannot reply to my nani' - so it will not travel in a family group chat, the only place with real reach. Their own kill line asks for just 100 of the first 1,000 signups from community sources, conceding that 90% must come from search or paid, and paid is closed at $20-$80 per payer against freemium ARPU.
parsed.strongest_defence: Diaspora-identity content is one of the most reliably viral zero-cost formats on Reels and TikTok, and the unit that travels is the format rather than any user's own recording - 'her voice is the flashcard' is a three-second hook - while 'learn Punjabi' and 'learn Gujarati' remain cheap, under-contested App Store search terms compared with the languages the big apps fight over.
parsed.verdict_reason: Institutional embedding points at the wrong generation and the core artifact is private and unshareable, so growth falls back on slow organic content and ASO.
